quarantined_leads.lead: Current-window reports said Republican Senator Tim Sheehy faced questions after helping Capitol Police remove protester Brian McGinnis from a Senate Armed Services hearing; the reports referenced an alleged injury to McGinnis and criminal charges against the protester.
quarantined_leads.source_title: Tim Sheehy confrontation at Senate hearing leaves protester injured and charged
quarantined_leads.subject_response: Sheehy said in a public response that Capitol Police were trying to remove an unruly protester, that he assisted to de-escalate the situation, and that the protester had been looking for a confrontation. No new statement from Sheehy or an ethics/law-enforcement body was located in the current window.
quarantined_leads.reason: The current-window material consists of a single low-reliability report and a derivative summary, while the underlying confrontation occurred in March and was already covered by AP and CBS. No new Senate Ethics action, criminal charge, court filing, or official complaint against Sheehy was located, and the current reports do not independently establish that Sheehy injured the protester. The lead is retained for follow-up, not treated as a current event or finding.
